note: The two sets are nearly identical; every claim in B also appears in A. A adds one further claim — that the blue shading in Figure 14 represents the trailing edge reinforcement — which is directly supported by the Figure 14 caption ('The blue shading represents the thickness of unidirectional spar caps ... and trailing edge reinforcement (made of unidirectional glass)'). All shared claims are faithful to the text layer with supporting quotes, so A is marginally better for the extra correct claim. Both sets repeat the same facts under several entity/attribute phrasings (spar cap material, trailing edge reinforcement material, aft shear web extent, shear web material, leading/trailing edge uniaxial glass).
remarks: Both sets restate the same underlying facts multiple times (e.g. spar cap material as 'pultruded carbon', 'carbon fiber' and 'carbon uniaxial'; aft shear web 50% span twice; shear web sandwich material twice), inflating claim counts without adding information. The 50% value is given as 'approximately 50%' in the source but reported as exactly 50% in both sets. Neither set captures the modal-frequency / BECAS / HAWC2-BeamDyn facts in the last paragraph, though those may be outside the sampled claim scope.
